text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — saw a regression on the quantized kernel selection path. INT4 picks on sm86 are thrashing when seq_len > 2048, latency spikes ~2.3x. Can't reproduce on sm90.
Maria Gomez: oof. any diffs in kernel heuristics or workspace calc?
Alex Chen: suspected hysteresis threshold in the autotuner. Repro script attached, small profile: 
```
model: llama-3-small q4_0
arch: sm86
seq_len: 256 -> 1024 -> 3072 (burst)
selected_kernel: int4_fast_pack (at 256/1024)
fallback_kernel: int8_safe_kernel (when latency>threshold)
obs: when burst seq>2048 autotuner flips repeatedly between int4_fast_pack and int4_slow_unroll -> cache churn
profile hotspot: matmul_systolic + kv_store_evictions
```
Jia Patel: kv cache evictions? Are we evicting on small worker pools due to workspace changes?
Alex Chen: yeah, eviction count jumps during the kernel flip. Seems like int4_fast_pack uses smaller workspace but a slightly different kv layout leading to more frequent GC of per-request KV segments.
Samir Rao: Could be the workspace heuristic: when autotuner measures throughput it assumes steady seq_len. Bursts confuse hysteresis. We should add sequence-aware smoothing or a short cooldown window before switching kernels.
Maria Gomez: can you share the raw perf numbers? want to see tokens/s and p95 latency across the window.
Alex Chen: paste: 
```
# sm86, 4xA100-like sim
seq=256: tokens/s=7500, p95=48ms
seq=1024: tokens/s=6800, p95=62ms
seq=3072: tokens/s=2100, p95=210ms (with kernel flip)
# sm90 (same config)
seq=3072: tokens/s=6500, p95=70ms
```
Jia Patel: wow big gap. sm90 kernel seems to handle long sequences better (likely different matmul kernel select + larger shared workspace).
Samir Rao: Proposed quick fixes: 1) Add seq_len rolling average into autotuner decision (like 10s window). 2) Add hysteresis multiplier when kv_eviction_rate>threshold. 3) Temp patch: prefer stable int8 kernel for bursts on sm86.
Alex Chen: implemented small PoC: if recent_seq_mean > 1500 -> bias to int8_safe_kernel with a cost penalty of +5% so we only pick it under bursts. Reduced flip count to 0 in repro.
Maria Gomez: nice. do we have unit test or e2e?
Alex Chen: pushed a test in perf-ci that simulates seq distribution and asserts <3 kernel switches/min. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/2345
infra-bot: Deploy queued to perf-canary: redwood/serving-runtime@canary-17945. Autotune flag `seq_smoothing_ms` set to 10000 for canary.
Jia Patel: longer-term: we should add per-arch tuning params: default hysteresis for sm86 = 1.8, sm90 = 1.2 and a per-model override map. Also log `kvcache_eviction_rate` to console metrics.
Samir Rao: Agree. Also consider making kernel selection simulate short-horizon bursts when measuring candidate kernels — i.e., benchmark at a few seq points (512/1024/3072) and compute a weighted score based on observed distribution.
Alex Chen: filing a perf ticket with repro and PoC patch: PERF-1298. I'll include sample trace and the autotuner telemetry.
Maria Gomez: thanks. schedule a 30m sync tomorrow? want to align on rollout flags and metric alerts.
Alex Chen: yep — 10:30am. I'll add agenda: tuning params, canary plan, perf-ci additions. :thumbsup:
Jia Patel: tagging ops to watch kvcache alarm during canary @ops-team
Samir Rao: one more note — monitor memory fragmentation on sm86; int4 pack path triggers different alloc patterns. Could be unrelated but worth watching.
Alex Chen: good call. I'll add a fragmentation gauge to the canary.
Maria Gomez: great. thanks all.
